regulatory_body: IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India)
regulation_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024 (IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024), Part C: claims under retail general insurance
summary: A surveyor must be allocated within 24 hours of claim intimation and the insured told the surveyor's details, role and duties. The surveyor reports within 15 days of allocation, and the insurer decides the claim within 7 days of the survey report. Losses of Rs 50,000 or more (motor) or Rs 1 lakh or more (other lines) need a licensed surveyor and loss assessor. A claim settled late carries interest at bank rate plus 2% from intimation to payment. No claim may be rejected or closed for want of documents or for late intimation, or for breach of a warranty or condition unrelated to the loss, and a rejection must quote the specific policy terms. Complaints go to the insurer's grievance officer (reply within 14 days), IRDAI's Bima Bharosa portal and the Insurance Ombudsman for claims up to Rs 50 lakh. Checked against a third-party copy of the circular; confirm against irdai.gov.in.

regulatory_body: IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India)
regulation_title: Master Circular on General Insurance Business, 2024 (IRDAI/NL/MSTCIR/MISC/90/06/2024): product design, pricing, Use & File and UIN
summary: Applies to every general insurance product and add-on. Design and rating must be on a sound, prudent underwriting and actuarial basis; pricing should be based on appropriate data and/or technical justification, allowing for risk exposure, experience (including unusually heavy or light catastrophe and large-loss years), reinsurance, reserves and expenses, and premium rates shall not be excessive, inadequate or unfairly discriminatory. The insurer's Product Management Committee (including the Chief Underwriting Officer and the Appointed Actuary; quorum of three plus the Appointed Actuary) approves products under Use & File, and a product or add-on can be sold only after it has a UIN. Retail product wordings and related documents must be on the insurer's website before launch or within seven days of the UIN, whichever is earlier. Motor third-party liability premium continues to be regulated under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the Central Government's rules. Read from a TaxGuru reproduction; confirm against irdai.gov.in.

regulatory_body: IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India)
regulation_title: Bharat Griha Raksha: standard home insurance product every general insurer must offer (as reported by Business Standard)
summary: IRDAI made Bharat Griha Raksha mandatory for every general insurer to offer from April 2021. It covers the home building (including garages, compound walls, solar panels, water tanks and permanent fixtures) and general contents against fire, explosion, lightning, earthquake, storm, cyclone, flood and inundation, landslide, impact damage, riot and malicious damage, terrorism, bursting or overflowing of water tanks, apparatus and pipes, and sprinkler leakage, plus theft within 7 days of and caused by an insured event. General contents are covered automatically at 20% of the building sum insured, up to Rs 10 lakh. The policy does not give a full waiver of under-insurance: claims are paid up to the declared sum insured rather than proportionately.

regulatory_body: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (Parliament of India)
regulation_title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Chapter XI (s.146-147, compulsory third-party insurance) and s.165-166 (Motor Accidents Claims Tribunals)
summary: No vehicle may be used in a public place without a policy against third-party risks (s.146). The policy must cover liability for death of or bodily injury to any person, and damage to third-party property, arising out of use of the vehicle in a public place, and death or injury to passengers of public service vehicles (s.147). State Governments set up Motor Accidents Claims Tribunals (s.165); the injured person, the property owner or the legal representatives of a deceased person apply for compensation to the tribunal where the accident happened or where the claimant lives or works (s.166). Third-party premium is set by Central Government rules, not by the insurer.

regulatory_body: Ministry of Labour and Employment (Parliament of India)
regulation_title: Employee's Compensation Act, 1923, s.4A: compensation to be paid when due; interest and penalty for default
summary: Compensation for a workplace injury falls due on the date of the accident. Where the employer (or its insurer) disputes the extent of liability, it must pay provisionally the amount it admits. If compensation is not paid within one month of falling due, the Commissioner must order simple interest at 12% a year and may add a penalty of up to 50% of the amount. Disputes are decided by the Commissioner for Employee's Compensation. Read from the lawx.in reproduction of the Act; confirm against indiacode.nic.in.

regulatory_body: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH)
regulation_title: AIS-156 Amendment 3: additional safety requirements for traction batteries of electric vehicles (as reported by EVreporter)
summary: After a series of electric two-wheeler fires, MoRTH set up an expert committee in May 2022 and notified Amendment 3 to AIS-156 on 27 September 2022, in two phases. Phase 1 (from 1 December 2022): pack traceability, an additional safety fuse, protection against regenerative braking, cell-to-cell spacing and a microprocessor-based battery management system with protection against overcurrent, overcharge, over-discharge, over-voltage, short circuit and over-temperature. Phase 2 (from 31 March 2023): thermal propagation testing so that a thermal runaway in one cell does not spread through the pack, an audio-visual warning of a thermal event, four temperature sensors in the BMS, IS 16893 cell testing and EMC testing of the BMS. Packs must be IPx7 compliant against water ingress. Secondary source; confirm against the MoRTH notification.

regulation_title: Drone Rules, 2021: third-party insurance of unmanned aircraft systems (as summarised by Khaitan & Co)
summary: The Ministry of Civil Aviation notified the Drone Rules, 2021 on 25 August 2021. The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and its rules apply to third-party insurance of unmanned aircraft systems, except nano drones, and to compensation for damage to life or property they cause. Drones are classed by weight as nano, micro, small, medium and large. Law-firm summary; confirm against the notified Rules and any amendment.

regulation_title: Directions under section 70B(6) of the Information Technology Act, 2000 on reporting cyber incidents (28 April 2022)
summary: Service providers, intermediaries, data centres, body corporates (which includes insurers) and Government organisations must report the cyber incidents listed in Annexure I, such as targeted scanning, compromise of critical systems, unauthorised access, data breaches and ransomware, to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing them or being told of them, by e-mail, phone or fax. The directions took effect 60 days after issue.

regulatory_body: MeitY (Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology)
regulation_title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and DPDP Rules, 2025 (as summarised by Hogan Lovells)
summary: MeitY notified the DPDP Rules, 2025 in November 2025, bringing the Act's core obligations in over a phased 12-18 month timeline. Consent to process personal data must be free, specific, informed, unambiguous and unconditional, and can be withdrawn as easily as it was given, after which the data must be deleted unless the law requires keeping it. On a personal data breach, the data fiduciary (such as an insurer holding policyholder and claims data) must inform the Data Protection Board without delay, send a detailed report within 72 hours, and notify affected individuals promptly. Law-firm summary; confirm each provision's commencement date.
